channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Democrats flip statehouses in midterm wave
item.description: The showing across the country that flipped Congress to Democratic control on Election Day also trickled down to the state and local level.

item.title: UK has 'new pair of eyes' in space as new military satellite enters orbit
item.description: The UK has a "new pair of eyes" in space after it launched a new military satellite into orbit, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) has announced.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed's grandparents reflect on his historic Senate win
item.description: Judy and Jan Johnson spoke with ABC News Live about how proud they are to see their grandson, Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, be elected to Senate.

item.title: Man charged with murder of missing woman whose whereabouts remain unknown
item.description: A man has been charged with the murder of a missing woman whose whereabouts remain unknown.

item.title: Secret Service finds man parked near White House with multiple firearms: Authorities
item.description: The suspect, Ronny Guanipa-Chrinos, allegedly made threats to kill President Donald Trump, according to DHS.

item.title: Trump says chief of staff Susie Wiles out, Stephen Miller will replace her
item.description: Trump said his top aide Stephen Miller will replace her in the job.

item.title: Latino vote helped thwart Texas Republicans' redistricting effort
item.description: Last year, the Republican-controlled Texas legislature redrew its congressional maps aimed at giving the GOP five more seats.

item.title: WATCH: Guide dog Eddie named 2026 American Humane Society Hero Dog
item.description: Eddie, a 3-year-old Labrador retriever, was honored for changing the life of his legally blind owner, Luis Rodriguez, through his work as a guide dog.

item.title: Deep forces are reshaping America's electoral map - and what it means for White House race
item.description: This week's American midterm was a once-in-a-lifetime result.

item.title: US attorney tasked with leading probe into Trump's foes resigns from DOJ
item.description: Jason Reding Quinones, the U.S. attorney tasked with leading a sweeping and controversial conspiracy probe targeting President Trump’s foes, has resigned from the DOJ.

item.title: Critical incident declared after car 'damaged by gunfire' - with two arrested
item.description: A critical incident has been declared in Swansea after a car was damaged by gunfire, police said.

item.title: Cornell faculty vote 'no confidence' in university leadership after alleged gang rape
item.description: Cornell University's Faculty Senate has approved a resolution declaring "no confidence" in the institution's leadership amid a crisis sparked by an alleged 2024 gang rape.

item.title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years in prison
item.description: In tonight's edition, cult leader Paul Mackenzie is sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murder of 190 children starved ‌to death on his orders. Also, in South Africa, activists warn that new data centres could put added pressure on already strained water and electricity supplies. And Senegal continues to celebrate the spirit of sport at the Youth Olympic Games.

item.title: Europe bomb hoaxes widen
item.description: The series of hoax bomb scares sent to several Irish media outlets and European airlines are likely part of a coordinated campaign of disruption, according to the Irish government. Dozens of commercial flights have been targetted by email with threats said to be over and above the typical hoax in specificty. Ireland's broadcaster RTE who's staff evacuated the premises this morning and several Italian airlines, say they received a mesage cliaming to be from a Russian extremist group calling itself the Fighters of the Male State, which denied its implication. France 24's Jean-Emile Jammine speaks to Eric Schouten, founder and CEO of Dyami Security Intelligence.

item.title: Pope Leo arrives in Uruguay for first stop on 12-day South America tour
item.description: Pope Leo touched down in Uruguay on Friday to begin a 12-day tour of South America that will also see him visit Argentina and Peru. The tour is seen as something of a homecoming for the pontiff who lived in Peru for almost two decades and holds joint US and Peruvian citizenship.

item.title: WATCH: $11.4M shipment of Nvidia cargo stolen from Oakland
item.description: Experts describe the computer hardware theft as a sophisticated cargo heist.

item.title: Trump announces immigration hardliner Stephen Miller as new chief of staff
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Friday said advisor Stephen Miller would become his new chief of staff. Miller has been instrumental in driving the Trump administration's mass deportation programme and faced particular criticism after the deadly shootings of two Minneapolis protesters by ICE agents in January.

item.title: Israel's Arab-led parties in spotlight after inconclusive election
item.description: Israel's center-right opposition has a chance to unseat Netanyahu — but backing of Arab-led parties will be key.

item.title: WATCH: Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed’s grandparents react to historic win in Michigan
item.description: Jan and Judy Johnson, grandparents of Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, join ABC News Live to reflect on his Senate victory, their blended interfaith family and the traditions that bring them together.

item.title: Boy, 6, dies in hospital after house fire that killed four members of his family
item.description: A six-year-old who sustained critical injuries during a house fire that killed four members of his family has also died, police said.

item.title: The incoming class of U.S. senators is full of historic firsts
item.description: From the first Native American woman elected to the U.S. Senate and the first Muslim who will join the upper chamber to the Senate's first Paralympian, voters elected historic candidates on Tuesday.

item.title: Connecticut Sen. Murphy discharged from hospital after stroke, goes to rehab facility
item.description: Connecticut Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy says he has been discharged from the hospital after suffering a stroke last weekend and will miss “several weeks” of votes in the Senate as he recovers in a rehabilitation facility

item.title: Trump's global health strategy is emerging. What will the Democratic Congress say?
item.description: The Trump Administration has ushered in a fundamental shift in the U.S. approach to global health aid. How will the newly elected Democratic Congress weigh in?

item.title: Midterms: A Maga PostMortem, Europe’s ‘Shape Shifting’ Protests
item.description: A World This Week ‘Mid Terms Special’ Gavin Lee is joined by panel of four distinguished international correspondents to assess the aftermath of the worst Republican election result since the 1970s, post Watergate. We ask, is peak MAGA over? What will now change at home and abroad? And who ends the week in pole position as Presidential frontrunner for 2028? We also consider the scale and scope of Europe Wide Protests: This week housing organisations, trade unions and activist groups from seven countries met in Paris issuing a joint call for demonstrations. Are the national protest movements becoming a coordinated European movement?

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: No one knows how many ballots are outstanding in Mississippi's Senate race
item.description: The razor-thin margin between GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom is shining a light on an election process in Mississippi that is among the slowest and most decentralized in the U.S.

item.title: A homegrown Georgia moderate and pragmatist: Is Senator Ossoff the future of the Democratic Party?
item.description: Is Senator Jon Ossoff the future of the Democratic Party? Following a resounding midterm victory in Georgia, a former Republican stronghold, the 39-year-old senator has emerged as a prominent figure as the Democrats look ahead to 2028 for their next presidential nominee. His natural confidence, polished media performances and ability to appeal to a diverse electorate have prompted comparisons with Barack Obama. Yet behind the excitement surrounding his national prospects lies a more complicated question: whether political momentum in the Senate necessarily translates into a presidential frontrunner.

item.title: Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as Trump's chief of staff
item.description: The change comes after sweeping Republican losses in the midterm elections.

item.title: Pope Leo begins a 12-day, 3-country South America tour after his cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo begins his first South American tour since lung cancer surgery. The 12-day journey takes him to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he spent two decades.

item.title: WATCH: Fall’s beautiful colors on display at Utah’s Zion National Park
item.description: You can see more about Zion and other national parks on "National Parks USA," streaming now on Disney+.

item.title: Health intel-sharing group warns industry in wake of cyberattack on French blood bank
item.description: A healthcare intelligence-sharing organization is warning its members to lock down systems following cyberattacks on cold storage systems, including a French blood bank.

item.title: What Trump’s midterms debacle could mean for US support for Ukraine
item.description: The Republican Party's crushing defeat in midterm elections has left Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky optimistic about future support for Kyiv and stronger transatlantic relations. But with US President Donald Trump retaining broad foreign policy powers, the Democratic majority in Congress may have limited scope to bring about substantial change.

item.title: WATCH: 1st look at Nat Geo's 'Wolves Up Close with Bertie Gregory'
item.description: The new National Geographic documentary follows Bertie Gregory to Canada's Hudson Bay as he captures rare wolf behaviors during the harsh Arctic winter.

item.title: US officials unveil $280K deal to help Puerto Rico face water and power crises
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has met with nonprofits in Puerto Rico as officials announced a $280,000 partnership to help the U.S. territory confront emergencies

item.title: US midterms mark 'the beginning of the end' for Trump, John Bolton says
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, John Bolton, who served as national security adviser to Donald Trump during his first term, called the US midterm results "the beginning of the end" for Trump's stranglehold on the Republican Party. Democrats regained control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate earlier this week, marking the Republicans' worst performance since the 1974 elections in the wake of the Watergate scandal.

item.title: Trump moves to make Oval Office a national monument to prevent future major changes
item.description: Trump indicated the proclamation would have to be ratified by Congress.

item.title: Prince Harry to appeal after privacy lawsuit against Daily Mail publisher dismissed
item.description: Prince Harry and other household names are appealing a judge's decision dismissing their privacy lawsuit against a newspaper group.

item.title: Europe: What we know about the hoax bomb threats disrupting flights
item.description: Dozens of European flights have been disrupted this week after bomb threats were sent in to various airports, with fighter planes escorting many civilian aircraft after threats were called in mid-flight.

item.title: British comedian Russell Brand found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults
item.description: British comedian Russell Brand was on Thursday, November 5, found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults by a London jury, including a 16-year-old girl. He now faces "significant" prison time, according to the judge.

item.title: Pressure mounts on US Defence chief Hegseth after Republican election rout
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth is under growing pressure, with victorious Democrats planning to target him in Congress and Republicans blaming the Iran war he championed for their election losses. President Donald Trump has stood by Hegseth so far, insisting he's doing "a very good job". But Trump and Vice President JD Vance have both blamed midterm election losses on the Iran war, for which Hegseth is a key advocate and spokesman.

item.title: 'Trump is a very dangerous person for the world': EU's former top diplomat Josep Borrell
item.description: In an interview with Talking Europe, the EU's former top diplomat Josep Borrell reacts to the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections, warning that US President Donald Trump is still "a very dangerous person for the world".

item.title: 'Chaos within aviation industry' as European air traffic hit by bomb threats
item.description: Officials across Europe reported a fresh slew of bomb threats against multiple flights on Friday, November 6, following a string of hoaxes that have caused flight diversions this week. Two broadcasters also received security threats, in a possible sign the menace was spreading beyond the skies. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi has more.

item.title: Wounded French protesters to sue interior minister over police brutality
item.description: Around ten demonstrators wounded at recent protests in France on Friday said they will sue Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez over police brutality. Student and cost-of-living protests in recent weeks have been marred by violence, including reports of police inflicting serious and lifechanging injuries on protesters – many of whom are minors.

item.title: Turkey to push for 'electrification' drive at COP31 as climate threats mount
item.description: COP31 host Turkey is set to push for a "electrification" drive to help meet global elergy demand as the UN climate conference kicks off in Antalya on Monday. The annual summit takes place this year under the shadow of a cost-of-living crisis fuelled by the war in the Middle East.

item.title: Jay Rockefeller, former West Virginia governor and US senator, dies at 89
item.description: Jay Rockefeller, the last member of his family’s political dynasty who served as West Virginia’s governor and later a longtime U.S. senator, has died

item.title: European flights and broadcasters are targeted with another wave of bomb threats
item.description: Officials across Europe reported a slew of bomb threats against multiple flights, following a string of hoaxes that caused flight diversions this week. Three broadcasters also received threats.

item.title: China keeps a close eye on US midterm shake-up
item.description: The US midterm elections have resulted in the Democratic Party taking control of both chambers of the US Congress, leaving Donald Trump as a lame duck president for the remainder of his term. Professor Steve Tsang of the SOAS China Institute tells FRANCE 24 that, while a weakened Trump could strengthen Beijing's negotiating position, the Chinese leadership is aware that Congress has relatively little sway over foreign policy and is keen to maintain warm personal ties between the two presidents.

item.title: Election 2026 live results: Raman promises smooth transition of power to LA mayor
item.description: Raman is poised to become the 44th mayor of the nation’s second-largest city.

item.title: Pope Leo embarks on Latin America trip with a first stop in Uruguay
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is kicking off a three-nation tour of Latin America on Friday, November 6, with a visit to Uruguay, the region’s least Catholic and most secular country, three weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery that had put the entire trip into question. After Uruguay, he will then go to Argentina and Peru. FRANCE 24's Hanna Roberts has more.

item.title: California governor to grant clemency to all 548 death row inmates in state
item.description: California's governor Gavy Newsom announced Thursday that he will commute all death sentences in the state to life without the possibility of parole. He said that "capital punishment is morally wrong." The state Supreme Court will have the final say in hundreds of those cases.

item.title: The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult is sentenced to 200 years in prison
item.description: Cult leader Paul Mackenzie was convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult after he ordered his followers to starve themselves to death in order to meet Jesus.

item.title: Katherine Ryan feels 'grief and relief' over Brand guilty verdict
item.description: Comedian Katherine Ryan has said she feels "grief and relief" after Russell Brand was convicted of rape and sexual assault.

item.title: The women who rode the blue wave
item.description: In this edition, we report on how the US midterms, which saw the Democrats make massive gains, also marked a series of historic firsts for women. Also the dark side to Bangkok's booming fertility industry, which attracts thousands of foreign patients seeking assistance from the Thai capital's state-of-the-art private clinics. Plus how an impoverished neighbourhood in El Salvador, once a no-go zone plagued by gang violence, is being transformed by women into a vibrant canvas for street art.

item.title: 'Too early to draw conclusions' as bomb threat hoaxes target European countries
item.description: Several Irish media outlets reported receiving bomb threats on Friday as a wave of hoax alerts that had so far mainly targeted airlines continued across Europe, with more than a dozen new flights affected. No explosives have been found in any of the incidents so far. European authorities are scrambling to identify the sources of the threats, as FRANCE 24's Brussels correspondent Dave Keating reports.

item.title: Paraguay's Peña offers resignation amid banking scandal, protests
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña submitted his resignation on Thursday, but Congress put it on hold as impeachment proceedings against him move forward. Peña is facing impeachment over a banking scandal that has affected millions of people and sparked protests, with thousands taking to the streets in recent days.

item.title: Trump’s stillborn diesel deal: Why Russian oil tankers are not heading to the US
item.description: The first oil tankers scheduled to deliver Russian diesel to the US under a deal between President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin have changed course and are no longer heading toward the US coast. It spells the end of an agreement announced with great fanfare before the midterms.

item.title: Is Israel opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot going to replace Benjamin Netanyahu?
item.description: In Israel, Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday, November 5, as the frontrunner to be tasked with forming a government. This comes after one of the two main parties representing ultra-Orthodox Jewish voters – a longtime ally of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition – declined to recommend any candidate for the task. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Jerusalem Noga Tarnopolsky reports.

item.title: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's future in question after midterms setback
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's future is in question after Tuesday's, November 3, midterms setback. On Thursday, November 5, he issued a video message vowing to fight efforts in Congress to impeach him and defending the ‌Iran war as “courageous and historic”. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.

item.title: Two dead after bus carrying schoolchildren crashes in France, officials say
item.description: A seven-year-old girl and an 18-year-old boy have been killed after a bus crashed in eastern France, French authorities said.

item.title: WATCH: Multiple water rescues amid flood emergencies in the South
item.description: A flood emergency is underway across multiple states in the South – triggering dozens of water rescues in Florida, Georgia and Tennessee in the middle of the night.

item.title: WATCH: These identical twin sisters speak at the same time
item.description: Danny New talks to identical twin sisters in Australia who are turning heads for their unique speech patterns.

item.title: Man jailed after he admitted murdering mother of seven 28 years ago
item.description: A man has been jailed for more than 10 years after he admitted to murdering a mother of seven who disappeared 28 years ago then disposing of her decomposed body in household waste.

item.title: Data centers took a beating in the midterm elections
item.description: Opposition to data centers was part of midterm races across the U.S., with campaigns featuring them in hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of TV ads and many winners pledging to clamp down on the energy-hungry behemoths

item.title: WATCH: Authorities reveal motive in Citibank complex shooting
item.description: Chilling surveillance video shows a gunman exchanging gunfire with a security guard after ramming a gate at a Citibank complex near Tampa and killing a woman having lunch, authorities say.

item.title: WATCH: Meet the man who's the new voice of Boston's Logan airport
item.description: Christopher Donisi, an HVAC pipe fitter, will be the man behind the first voice travelers hear when they land in Beantown in the near future.

item.title: WATCH: Jaguars face injury-ravaged Ravens in Thursday Night Football matchup
item.description: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler previews the Jaguars-Ravens matchup, Baltimore’s quarterback injuries and Trevor Lawrence’s strong start to the season.

item.title: WATCH: Bob Dylan, Prince William, Prince Harry: Here's what's trending
item.description: ABC News' Rocsi Diaz takes a look at what's buzzing, including Bob Dylan meeting with Pope Leo at the Vatican and Prince William and Prince Harry joining forces to honor their mother.

item.title: Breakaway league LIV Golf to fold after filing for bankruptcy
item.description: Breakaway men's league LIV Golf is to fold instead of launching a new version because of a lack of financial support.

item.title: Family of footballer who died after on-pitch collision pay tribute to him
item.description: Family, friends and teammates gathered for the funeral of the Spanish footballer who died following an on-field collision with another player.

item.title: Meghan's brother a 'person of interest' in child abuse image claims
item.description: Meghan Markle's half brother has been named as a "person of interest" in an investigation into child sexual abuse image allegations against the Duchess of Sussex's father.

item.title: WATCH: Fuel prices drop after midterm elections
item.description: Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, explains what's behind the decrease in prices.
